summary: Iteration 2 testing complete. 47/47 backend pytest cases pass (15 new + 32 regression after updating two iter-1 tests for the new real-email contract). Frontend: login signup link removed, /signup redirects to /login, forgot-password flow no longer leaks debug OTP and advances to step 2 with toast, teacher sidebar has Students item between My Classes and Attendance, /teacher/students shows class tabs (5-A/5-B/6-A) + Add student modal opens, Lost & Found Report-item modal contains JPEG/PNG image upload field. Real Resend email confirmed via backend.err.log (Email sent id=... lines for forgot-password, lost-found claimed, lost-found resolved). Same-status update does NOT re-trigger email. Teacher (non-admin) can update lost-found status. File upload accepts JPEG/PNG, rejects non-image (400) and >5MB (400); download works with Bearer header and ?auth= query, returns 401 without token.

minor.issue: Parent demo password hash in Mongo did NOT match parent123 at start of run — login returned 401. Had to manually re-hash via auth_utils.hash_password and update DB before parent-token-dependent tests could run. Likely caused by an earlier reset-password test that stomped the parent demo user, OR the seed uses a different bcrypt cost on each run. seed.run_seed should idempotently upsert demo passwords. Same risk flagged in iteration_1.

action_items: Make seed.run_seed idempotent for demo passwords (admin/teacher/parent) — re-upsert password_hash on every startup so a reset-password or stale hash cannot lock out demo accounts.
Consider extending the same idempotent re-seed to demo user 'name' (still drifting due to /api/profile updates from past tests).
Optional: emit stronger structured logging (JSON) for emails so future tests don't have to grep raw text 'Email sent (id=...)' from supervisor stderr.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py forgot-password leaks user existence indirectly: success vs. 'If the email exists' message — current implementation returns the existence-safe message only on miss but a 'Reset code sent — please check your email.' on hit. Either both should be identical, or revert to always-OK. Currently only an information-leak in error responses, low severity.

files.py download endpoint accepts the access JWT in a query string (?auth=) for rendering — JWT will end up in browser history / referer headers. Acceptable trade-off but document or use short-lived signed URLs in a future iteration.

storage_service.put_object/get_object are synchronous wrapped via asyncio.to_thread — fine, but 403-refresh logic uses module-level _storage_key without locking around the second call; two concurrent uploads after token expiry could race-init twice. Low impact.

shared.py update_lost_found: state-transition guard is correct (open->claimed triggers email, claimed->claimed does not), but resolved->claimed would also trigger a 'claimed' email even though the prior state was already terminal. Consider restricting transitions to forward-only.
files.py /upload accepts up to 5MB but reads the entire body into memory before size check — under load, large-payload DoS is possible. Use Content-Length header pre-check or stream-and-abort.
JWT still in localStorage as 'sc_token' (carried over from iter 1) and there is still no rate-limit / brute-force lockout on /api/auth/login (playbook expectation).

rca of the issue: Parent demo login 401 at test start — DB password_hash for parent@school.com no longer matched 'parent123'. Reproduce: curl POST /api/auth/login parent@school.com/parent123 -> 401. Mitigation applied: hashed parent123 with auth_utils.hash_password and updated users collection.
